title: CBSE Class 12 Computer Science · Practice paper 3
subject: Computer Science
label: Practice paper
instr: All questions are compulsory. However, internal choices have been provided in some questions. Attempt only one of the choices in such questions.
The paper is divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
Section A consists of 21 questions (1 to 21). Each question carries 1 mark.
Section B consists of 7 questions (22 to 28). Each question carries 2 marks.
Section C consists of 3 questions (29 to 31). Each question carries 3 marks.
Section D consists of 4 questions (32 to 35). Each question carries 4 marks.
Section E consists of 2 questions (36 and 37). Each question carries 5 marks.
All programming questions are to be answered using Python Language only.
In case of MCQ, text of the correct answer should also be written.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Write the output on execution of the following Python code:
s = "Board2027"
print(s.isalpha(), s[5:].isdigit())
questions.model:
s contains digits, so isalpha() is False. s[5:] is "2027", which has only digits, so isdigit() is True.
False True

points.t: Correct output: False True

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following code?
words = ["red", "green", "blue"]
print("-".join(words).upper())
questions.sol: join() places "-" between the words (not after the last one) and gives "red-green-blue"; upper() then converts it to capital letters.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which of the following creates a tuple containing the single element 7?
questions.sol: A comma is needed to make a tuple of one element: (7,). (7) is just the integer 7 in brackets, [7] is a list and {7} is a set.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which query displays the number of different cities in the City column of the table EMP?
options: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM EMP GROUP BY City;
questions.sol: DISTINCT inside COUNT() makes MySQL count each different city only once. COUNT(City) counts every non-NULL city, including repeated ones; DISTINCT COUNT(City) still gives that single count; COUNT(*) with GROUP BY City gives the number of employees in each city (one row per city), not the number of cities.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following code?
L = [1, 2, 3]
M = L
M.append(4)
print(L, L is M)
questions.sol: M = L does not copy the list; both names refer to the same list object. So the change made through M is seen in L, and L is M is True.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What possible output is expected to be displayed on the screen at the time of execution of the following code?
import random
s = "PYTHON"
i = random.randint(0, 2)
j = random.randint(3, 5)
print(s[i:j])
questions.sol: i can be 0, 1 or 2 and j can be 3, 4 or 5; the slice stops before index j. With i = 1 and j = 5 the output is YTHO. HON needs i = 3, and PYTHON and THON need j = 6, which are not possible.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following code?
d = {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}
x = d.pop("b")
d["d"] = x * 5
print(d)
questions.sol: pop("b") removes the key "b" and returns its value 2. Then the new key "d" gets 2 * 5 = 10.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which cable has a copper wire at its core that is surrounded by insulating material, which in turn is surrounded by an outer conductor (usually a copper mesh)?
questions.sol: A co-axial cable has a central copper wire, an insulating layer, and an outer conductor of copper mesh, all covered with plastic. This shielding protects the signal from interference.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which query will display the names of the employees who are NOT from Delhi or Mumbai, from the table EMP(Name, City)?
options: SELECT Name FROM EMP WHERE City NOT IN ('Delhi', 'Mumbai');
SELECT Name FROM EMP WHERE City != 'Delhi' OR City != 'Mumbai';
SELECT Name FROM EMP WHERE City NOT BETWEEN 'Delhi' AND 'Mumbai';
SELECT Name FROM EMP WHERE City IN NOT ('Delhi', 'Mumbai');
questions.sol: NOT IN excludes every row whose city is in the list. Option B is true for every row (no city can be both), C compares alphabetical ranges, and D is not valid syntax.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following Python statement?
print(2 ** 3 ** 2 % 10 + 7 / 2)
questions.model:
** is evaluated from right to left: 3 ** 2 = 9, 2 ** 9 = 512. Then 512 % 10 = 2 and 7 / 2 = 3.5. 2 + 3.5 = 5.5.
5.5

points.t: Correct output: 5.5

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a logical error in a Python program?
options: Missing colon at the end of an if statement
Using + in place of * in the formula for the area of a rectangle
Dividing a number by zero while the program runs
Writing the keyword while as whiel
questions.sol: A logical error lets the program run but gives a wrong result, as with a wrong operator in a formula. A and D are syntax errors; C is a run-time error.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of data communication?
questions.sol: The components of data communication are sender, receiver, message, communication medium and protocols. A compiler is a language translator, not a part of data communication.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of storing data in a database instead of separate files?
options: Data can be shared by many users
More copies of the same data have to be kept up to date
questions.sol: A DBMS reduces redundancy and keeps data consistent and shareable. Having to keep many copies of the same data up to date is a problem of the file system, not an advantage of a database.

questions.subject: Computer Science

What will be the output of the following Python code?
def f(n):
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return n // 2, "even"
    return n * 3, "odd"

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R) based question. Mark the correct choice as:
(A) Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
(B) Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.
(C) A is True but R is False.
(D) A is False but R is True.
Assertion (A): While reading all the records of a binary file, pickle.load() is usually written in a loop inside a try block that has an except EOFError clause.
Reason (R): pickle.load() raises an EOFError when it tries to read after the last record of the file.
options: Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.
A is True but R is False.
A is False but R is True.
questions.sol: Both are true. Since load() raises EOFError at the end of the file, the except EOFError clause is used to stop the reading loop: R explains A.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R) based question. Mark the correct choice as:
(A) Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
(B) Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.
(C) A is True but R is False.
(D) A is False but R is True.
Assertion (A): After a SELECT query is executed through a cursor, cursor.fetchone() returns None when no more rows are left to be fetched.
Reason (R): fetchone() returns all the remaining rows of the result as a list of tuples.
options: Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.
A is True but R is False.
A is False but R is True.
questions.sol: A is true: fetchone() returns the next row as a tuple, or None when no rows are left. R is false: it is fetchall() that returns all the remaining rows as a list of tuples.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A. Differentiate between a text file and a binary file. (Write any two points.)
questions.model:
Text file: stores data as characters that a person can read (for example, in Notepad); each line ends with an end-of-line (newline) character. It is opened in modes such as r, w and a.
Binary file: stores data in the same form as it is held in memory (bytes), so its contents cannot be read directly by a person; there is no line structure. It is opened in modes such as rb, wb and ab, and the pickle module is used to write and read Python objects.

points.t: Any one correct point of difference (e.g. human-readable characters vs bytes)
Any second correct point (e.g. lines ending in newline vs no lines; r/w modes vs rb/wb modes with pickle)

or.text: B. Differentiate between an absolute path and a relative path of a file, with an example of each.
or.model:
An absolute path gives the complete location of a file starting from the root (drive), for example: C:\School\Reports\marks.txt
A relative path gives the location of a file with respect to the current working folder, for example: Reports\marks.txt (when the current folder is C:\School).

points.t: Correct difference: absolute starts from the root; relative is from the current folder
Correct example of an absolute path
Correct example of a relative path

or.text:
B. Write a Python function count_ds(s) that takes a string s and returns two values: the number of digits and the number of spaces in s.
Example: count_ds("Hello World 2027") should return (4, 2).
or.model:
def count_ds(s):
    digits = 0
    spaces = 0
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isdigit():
            digits += 1
        elif ch == " ":
            spaces += 1
    return digits, spaces

points.t: Correct function header
Correct loop with isdigit() and the check for a space, using two counters
Returning both values

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Predict the output of the following Python code:
nums = [12, 7, 30, 45, 8, 21]
i = 0
out = []
while i < len(nums):
    if nums[i] % 3 == 0:
        out.append(nums[i] // 3)
        i += 2
    else:
        out.append(nums[i] % 5)
        i += 1
print(out)
questions.model:
i = 0: 12 is divisible by 3, append 4, i = 2. i = 2: 30, append 10, i = 4. i = 4: 8 is not divisible by 3, append 8 % 5 = 3, i = 5. i = 5: 21, append 7, i = 7 and the loop ends.
[4, 10, 3, 7]

points.t: Values 4 and 10 (elements 7 and 45 are skipped)
Complete output [4, 10, 3, 7]

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Write suitable commands to do the following in MySQL.
I. Create a table MEMBER with the columns MID (integer, primary key), MName (variable-length string of up to 30 characters, which cannot be left empty) and JoinDate (date).
II. Insert the record 101, Ishaan, 1 July 2026 into the table MEMBER.
questions.model:
I. CREATE TABLE MEMBER (MID INT PRIMARY KEY, MName VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, JoinDate DATE);
II. INSERT INTO MEMBER VALUES (101, 'Ishaan', '2026-07-01');

II. Correct INSERT with the date written as 'YYYY-MM-DD'

or.text: B. Differentiate between the PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints in MySQL with a suitable example.
or.model:
PRIMARY KEY: the column must have unique values and cannot contain NULL; a table can have only one primary key. UNIQUE: the column must have unique values but it can contain NULL; a table can have more than one UNIQUE column.
Example: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (AdmNo INT PRIMARY KEY, Email VARCHAR(40) UNIQUE, Name VARCHAR(30));

points.t: Correct difference: NULL not allowed in primary key but allowed in UNIQUE; only one primary key per table
Correct example showing both constraints

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A. Differentiate between HTML and XML. (Write any two points.)
questions.model:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is used to design web pages and display data; it has predefined tags such as <p> and <table>.
XML (Extensible Markup Language) is used to store and carry data; its tags are not predefined but are defined by the user.

points.t: Purpose: HTML displays data (web pages); XML stores and transports data
Tags: predefined in HTML; user-defined in XML

or.text:
B. I. What is a gateway?
II. How is a switch different from a hub?
or.model:
I. A gateway is a device that connects two different networks (which may use different protocols) and lets them communicate, by translating the data between them.
II. A hub sends the data it receives to all the devices connected to it, while a switch sends the data only to the device for which it is meant.

points.t: I. Correct meaning of gateway
II. Hub sends data to all devices; switch only to the intended device

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Write and call a Python function AvgWords() that reads all the lines of the text file "Speech.txt" using readlines() and displays the average number of words per line.
For example, if the file contains:
Good morning to all
Today we talk about water
Save every drop
the function should display:
Average words per line: 4.0
questions.model:
def AvgWords():
    f = open("Speech.txt", "r")
    lines = f.readlines()
    f.close()
    total = 0
    for line in lines:
        total = total + len(line.split())
    avg = total / len(lines)
    print("Average words per line:", avg)

AvgWords()

points.t: Correct function header
Opening the file and reading it with readlines()
Correct logic: total words using split() and division by the number of lines
Correctly calling the function

or.text: B. Write a Python function RemoveBlank() that reads the text file "Draft.txt" and copies all its lines, except the blank lines, into a new file "Clean.txt". A blank line is a line that has nothing other than spaces and the newline character.
or.model:
def RemoveBlank():
    fin = open("Draft.txt", "r")
    fout = open("Clean.txt", "w")
    for line in fin:
        if line.strip() != "":
            fout.write(line)
    fin.close()
    fout.close()

points.t: Correct function header
Opening Draft.txt in read mode and Clean.txt in write mode
Correct check for a blank line using strip()
Writing the non-blank lines and closing the files

The maximum temperatures of some cities on a summer day are stored as a list of tuples (City, Temperature):
readings = [("Jaisalmer", 46), ("Shimla", 22),
            ("Nagpur", 44), ("Pune", 35),
            ("Banda", 47)]

Correct push of the city name

parts.q:

For the data above, after push_hot(Hot, readings), four calls of pop_city(Hot) should return Banda, Nagpur, Jaisalmer and Underflow, in this order.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Predict the output of the following Python code:
x = 10
def outer(y):
    global x
    x = x + y
    z = x * 2
    return z

def show():
    x = 3
    print("in show:", x)

w = outer(5)
show()
print(x, w)
questions.model:
outer(5) uses the global x: x becomes 15, z = 30 is returned, so w = 30. In show(), x = 3 creates a local variable, so it prints "in show: 3" and the global x stays 15.
in show: 3
15 30

points.t: First line: in show: 3
Second line: 15
30 on the second line

or.text:
B. Write a Python function merge_dict(d1, d2) that takes two dictionaries whose values are numbers and returns a new dictionary containing all the keys of both. For a key present in both, the value should be the sum of the two values. The dictionary d1 must not be changed.
Example: merge_dict({'a': 5, 'b': 3}, {'b': 4, 'c': 9}) should return {'a': 5, 'b': 7, 'c': 9}.
or.model:
def merge_dict(d1, d2):
    result = d1.copy()
    for k in d2:
        if k in result:
            result[k] = result[k] + d2[k]
        else:
            result[k] = d2[k]
    return result

points.t: Correct function header
Making a new dictionary (copy of d1 or empty) so that d1 is not changed
Correct loop: adding values for common keys and inserting new keys
Returning the new dictionary

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A cab service stores the details of its trips in a CSV file named Trips.csv (without a header row). Each record has the columns:
TripID, Driver, Km, Fare
For example: T2,Salma,72,860
Write the following user-defined functions:

parts.q: I. count_driver(name): to count and return the number of trips made by the driver whose name is passed as name.
parts.model:
import csv
def count_driver(name):
    f = open("Trips.csv", "r")
    r = csv.reader(f)
    c = 0
    for row in r:
        if row[1] == name:
            c += 1
    f.close()
    return c

points.t: Opening the file in read mode
Correctly creating the reader object
Correct comparison of the Driver column with name
Correct counting and return

parts.q: II. longest_trip(): to display the TripID and Driver of the trip with the longest distance (Km). (Assume that no two trips have the same distance.)
parts.model:
import csv
def longest_trip():
    f = open("Trips.csv", "r")
    r = csv.reader(f)
    maxkm = 0
    for row in r:
        if int(row[2]) > maxkm:
            maxkm = int(row[2])
            tid = row[0]
            drv = row[1]
    f.close()
    print(tid, drv)

points.t: Opening the file in read mode and creating the reader object
Correct loop over the rows with Km converted to int
Correct logic to keep the largest distance with its TripID and Driver
Displaying the TripID and Driver

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A school library stores the details of its books in a binary file Books.dat. Each record is a list [BookID, Title, Copies], where Copies is the number of copies available in the library. Write Python functions to:

parts.q:
I. create_books(): create the file Books.dat and write the following four records into it, one record at a time:
[1, "Wings of Fire", 3], [2, "Malgudi Days", 1], [3, "Gitanjali", 0], [4, "Panchatantra", 5]
parts.model:
import pickle
def create_books():
    data = [[1, "Wings of Fire", 3],
            [2, "Malgudi Days", 1],
            [3, "Gitanjali", 0],
            [4, "Panchatantra", 5]]
    f = open("Books.dat", "wb")
    for rec in data:
        pickle.dump(rec, f)
    f.close()

points.t: Correct function header
Opening the file in write binary mode (wb)
Writing each record using pickle.dump() in a loop
Closing the file

parts.q: II. reorder(): copy all the records whose Copies is less than 2 from Books.dat into another binary file Reorder.dat, and return the number of records copied. (For the records above it should return 2.)
parts.model:
import pickle
def reorder():
    fin = open("Books.dat", "rb")
    fout = open("Reorder.dat", "wb")
    n = 0
    try:
        while True:
            rec = pickle.load(fin)
            if rec[2] < 2:
                pickle.dump(rec, fout)
                n += 1
    except EOFError:
        fin.close()
        fout.close()
    return n
Note: import pickle may be written once for the whole program.

points.t: Opening Books.dat in rb mode and Reorder.dat in wb mode
Using pickle.load() in a loop with try-except EOFError
Correct condition Copies less than 2 and writing the record with dump()
Counting and returning the number of records copied

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Indus Valley College is setting up a new campus in Shillong. Its head office is in New Delhi. The campus has four blocks: LIBRARY, SCIENCE, ARTS and HOSTEL. As a network expert, suggest the best solutions for the questions (I) to (V), keeping in mind the distances and other details given below.
Distance between the blocks:
FromToDistance
LIBRARYSCIENCE45 m
LIBRARYARTS60 m
LIBRARYHOSTEL150 m
SCIENCEARTS75 m
SCIENCEHOSTEL95 m
ARTSHOSTEL110 m
Number of computers in each block:
BlockComputers
LIBRARY20
SCIENCE110
ARTS50
HOSTEL30

parts.q: I. Suggest the most suitable block to install the server, with a suitable reason.
parts.model: SCIENCE, because it has the maximum number of computers (110).

points.t: SCIENCE with the reason: maximum number of computers

parts.q: II. Draw the cable layout to connect all the blocks efficiently, using a star topology with the server block at the centre. Is a repeater needed in this layout? Justify.
parts.model: Star layout with SCIENCE at the centre: SCIENCE to LIBRARY (45 m), SCIENCE to ARTS (75 m) and SCIENCE to HOSTEL (95 m). No repeater is needed, because every cable in this layout is shorter than 100 m.

points.t: Star layout with SCIENCE at the centre connected to the other three blocks (drawn or described)
No repeater, as all cables are shorter than 100 m

parts.q: III. Give one reason why a star topology is preferred to a bus topology for this campus.
parts.model: In a star topology each block has its own cable to the centre, so a fault in one cable affects only that block; in a bus topology a fault in the main (backbone) cable stops the whole network. (Also accepted: the network can be managed centrally from the server block; a fault is easy to find; a new block is easy to add.)

points.t: Correct reason, e.g. failure of one cable does not stop the whole network, unlike a break in the bus backbone (or central management / easy fault finding / easy extension)

parts.q: IV. The students in the HOSTEL want to use their laptops anywhere in the building without cables. Which wireless technology should be set up in the HOSTEL, and which device must be installed in the building to create it?
parts.model: Wi-Fi (wireless LAN). Access points (APs) must be installed in the building (on each floor), connected to the wired network of the block, for example to its switch.

points.t: Wi-Fi (wireless LAN)
Access point (AP)

parts.q: V. A. The students want to download their e-mail from the college mail server to their own computers. Which protocol is used to retrieve e-mail from a mail server?

points.t: POP3

or.q: V. B. The link to the head office has a data transfer rate of 100 Mbps. What does Mbps stand for, and what does the data transfer rate of a link measure?
or.model: Mbps stands for megabits per second. The data transfer rate is the number of bits transmitted between the sender and the receiver in one second (also called the bit rate).

points.t: Mbps: megabits per second
Data transfer rate: number of bits transmitted between sender and receiver per second
